title: Tool API naming adapter and call compatibility layer
creator: Avery Stone
description: Implement a compatibility adapter that allows OpenAI-style tool descriptions (name, description, json_schema parameters) to be invoked against Redwood's legacy function surface and runtime. The adapter must: map tool names to function identifiers, translate structured parameter objects into legacy positional/typed args, preserve streaming semantics where possible, and emit telemetry for mismatches. This enables customers using OpenAI-style tool calling to migrate to Redwood without rewriting large parts of their handler codebase.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter resolves OpenAI tool name -> Redwood function id with deterministic namespace rules
Adapter translates JSON Schema parameters into legacy argument list and performs type coercion or graceful rejection with clear error codes
Streaming from the model to the client is preserved when functions emit partial outputs; adapter supports streaming function output and incremental KV cache updates
Compatibility layer logs a deprecation warning for any legacy function name collisions and suggests canonical names
Automated test suite covering name collisions, missing params, extra params, enum coercions, and streaming edge cases with >= 95% pass rate
Performance overhead for the adapter is under 3ms median added latency on the hot path for typical requests (95th percentile under 15ms)
Feature gated and rolloutable by customer with telemetry flags for opt-in/out and staged migration
tasks: Design name resolution rules and lookup table format (owner: Priya)
Implement mapping library: tool->function, parameter translation, and type coercion (owner: Backend team)
Extend runtime to accept translated invocation envelope and preserve streaming semantics (owner: Runtime team)
Add telemetry hooks: mismatch counters, coercion occurrences, latency impact (owner: Observability)
Create migration CLI to generate mapping suggestions from existing function registry (owner: Tools)
Write unit/integration tests and synthetic benchmarks (owner: QA)
Prepare rollout plan and customer docs for migration (owner: Developer Experience)
Security review for input translation edge cases (owner: Security)
Create canary configuration and enable feature flag support in Console (owner: Console)
Add e2e test that simulates OpenAI-style call from SDK -> adapter -> legacy function -> streamed client response (owner: E2E)
design_decisions: Prefer a conservative mapping for names: normalize to kebab-case and namespace by customer_id when provided to avoid global collisions
Adopt tolerant parameter parsing by default: coerce strings->numbers/booleans where safe, validate enums strictly and return structured error when invalid
Expose strict mode via mapping config for customers who require deterministic validation
Streaming: do not buffer full function output in adapter. Use a passthrough stream that annotates fragments with adapter provenance to preserve ordering and low latency
Telemetry: surface an aggregated migration_score metric per customer to prioritize support and rollout interventions
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal teams only, feature flag enabled (duration: 1 week)
Beta: opt-in customers with migration support (duration: 3 weeks)
Canary: 5% of production traffic for selected customers, monitor metrics and error budget (duration: 1 week)
Gradual ramp: increase to 25% -> 50% -> 100% if metrics stable, with rollback hooks
Documentation and migration CLI published before 50% ramp
Post-ramp retrospective and migration playbook for enterprise customers
test_plan: Unit tests for name normalization, mapping table lookups, and ambiguous name resolution
Integration tests covering parameter translation, missing/extra fields, and enum coercion
Streaming e2e that asserts partial outputs are delivered within latency SLOs and in correct order
Load test with mixed OpenAI-tool and native Redwood function calls to quantify overhead
Fuzz tests to detect injection-like edge cases in parameter translation
Security-focused regression tests for strict mode and coercion paths
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: name collisions causing incorrect function invocations. Mitigation: namespaced resolution, explicit mapping, and strong telemetry to detect anomalies
Risk: adapter introduces tail latency. Mitigation: microbenchmarks, optimized hot path, and fallback to direct legacy invocation when latency threshold exceeded
Risk: data loss in streaming conversion. Mitigation: streaming passthrough with sequence markers and test coverage for partial emissions
Risk: mismatches silently tolerated lead to incorrect behaviour. Mitigation: default tolerant parsing + opt-in strict mode and audit logs for all coercions
